ios.desc:
# H for Hacker News – A Better Way to Read Hacker News

H for Hacker News is a fast, modern, and beautifully designed Hacker News client. Stay updated with the latest in technology, startups, programming, AI, and more — all in one intuitive and clutter-free app.

Key Features

# Search and Discover

- Search across the entire Hacker News archive
- Easily find and bookmark high-quality discussions

# Full Content Access

- Browse Top, New, Best, Show HN, Ask HN, and Job stories
- Read full threads with a clean, collapsible comment view
- View user profiles, karma scores, and submission history

# Advanced Bookmarking

- Save stories into custom collections
- Organize your bookmarks by topic or interest
- Quickly return to your favorite reads

# Efficient and Seamless Browsing

- Infinite scrolling for uninterrupted exploration
- Optimized for fast loading and smooth navigation
- Minimal data usage, even on slow connections

# Unified Reading Experience

- Read articles and comments in one integrated view
- Built-in reader for external links
- Share stories easily through messaging and social apps

# Full Control Over Your Data

- Export and import your bookmarks and reading history
- Your data stays with you — no tracking, no lock-in

# Read History

- Automatically keeps a timeline of everything you've read
- Easily revisit past stories and discussions

# Why Choose H for Hacker News?


Built for developers, entrepreneurs, and tech enthusiasts, H for Hacker News delivers the best of Hacker News in a distraction-free, performance-optimized app that fits your workflow.

quotes.text:
hey HN,

I am re launching an HN client app that i built this year. It got very little traction when i launched earlier.  Following YC advice to do multiple launches, I am going to give it another shot.

It’s fairly basic, but here are some of the features that I hope you would like.

- Minimal, distraction-free UI

- keyword based search functionality to see past stories.

- Dark mode support

- Breeze through comments with collapse functionality.

- Bookmark your favourite stories to read later or revisit any time

- All your reading history is saved.

- Export reading history when you want it.

I hope you give it a try! The app is free with an optional contribution for those who wish to do it.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/h-for-hacker-news/id6744145932

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I'm the creator of Libris.fm. I've been a long-time fan of audiobooks, especially classic literature found in the public domain. I wanted a simple, dedicated app to listen to these works narrated by real people, without any distractions.

Libris.fm brings together over 10,000 human-narrated audiobooks, primarily sourced from LibriVox and the Internet Archive.

Key points:

Completely Free: No subscriptions or paywalls.

No Ads & No Tracking: Built with privacy in mind. Just the books.

Human Narration: Focused specifically on volunteer-read recordings, not synthetic voices.

Simple Interface: Includes essentials like background playback, speed adjustment, and skip controls.

Content: Lots of classic literature, poetry, history, drama, etc. Please checkout the discover screen and see for yourself.

This was a passion project born out of my love for literature and a belief that these public domain works deserve to be easily accessible. It's not trying to be an Audible or Spotify competitor, but rather a focused tool for enjoying these specific types of audiobooks.

It's currently available here: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/h-for-hacker-news/id6744145932

I'm actively developing it and would genuinely appreciate any feedback from the HN community – feature requests, bug reports, or general thoughts are all welcome!
